recipe: Prefer `.textContent` or jQuery's `$.text()` over `.innerHTML` or `$.html()` when rendering user input to avoid XSS. If you must render raw HTML, escape the contents first.
trigger_condition: You need to render user-generated input in the DOM during a UI coding task.
evidence: You almost never need to use `.innerHTML` or jQuery's `$.html()`. There's `.textContent` and `$.text()`. If you do have to render raw HTML, make sure you escape the contents first.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Encode user input before displaying it in the URL to prevent users from injecting additional query parameters.
trigger_condition: You are constructing a URL that includes user-supplied values.
evidence: User input that is being displayed in the URL has to be encoded first as well, or else there's also a potential for mischief where users can add additional query parameters.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Always render an explicit empty state when a list or collection has zero items instead of showing nothing.
trigger_condition: Your component renders a dynamic list of items that may be empty.
evidence: What if there are no items, what do you show? Hint: show an empty state to indicate absence of contents. Do not show nothing.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: When a list can contain an unbounded number of items, set a max height or implement pagination to prevent layout breakage.
trigger_condition: Your component renders a list whose length is determined at runtime and could be very large.
evidence: What if there are too many items? Hint: set max height or paginate.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Apply the CSS `word-break` property to handle strings that are too long for their container.
trigger_condition: Your component may receive user input or data that is longer than the available space allows.
evidence: What if a string is too long? Hint: CSS `word-break` property.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Batch your data fetches to avoid spamming the API endpoint when loading a large amount of data or images.
trigger_condition: Your component needs to load a lot of data or images from an API.
evidence: Can you fetch the data in batches to reduce spamming the API endpoint?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Lazily load data or images that are not immediately visible to reduce initial load time.
trigger_condition: Your component needs to load a lot of data or images that are not all needed at once.
evidence: Can you lazily load them? Can you fetch the data in batches to reduce spamming the API endpoint?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Handle race conditions in async requests by ensuring a new network request does not overwrite the result of a previous in-flight request.
trigger_condition: Your component fires multiple network or async requests that may complete out of order.
evidence: Does the component deal with race conditions in network/async requests? E.g. a new network request is fired before the response for the previous request is returned.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Implement graceful recovery for network timeouts and errors so the component remains usable when a request fails.
trigger_condition: Your component depends on network requests that can time out or return an error.
evidence: What if the request times out or errors out? How can you recover from it gracefully?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Consider using caching, lazy loading, or prefetching/preloading to improve component performance.
trigger_condition: Your component makes network requests and you want to optimize its loading performance.
evidence: How can you improve the performance of the component? Can you make use of caching, lazy loading, prefetching/preloading?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Ensure multiple instances of the same component on a page are fully independent and do not share mutable state.
trigger_condition: Your component may be instantiated multiple times on the same page.
evidence: Will having multiple components on the same page affect each other? They should be independent!
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Avoid hard-coding values that will make it difficult to extend the component to changing requirements; design for extensibility from the start.
trigger_condition: You are building a reusable UI component that may need to adapt to future requirements.
evidence: Did you hard code any values that will make it hard to extend to changing requirements in future? Did you design for extensibility?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions

recipe: Incorporate basic accessibility practices including text size, color contrast, focusable elements, tab focus order, and `aria-label`s into your component.
trigger_condition: You are building a UI component and want to meet minimum accessibility standards.
evidence: You should be at least aware of basic a11y practices like text size, color contrast, focusable elements, tab focus order, `aria-label`s.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: User Interface coding questions
